items.briefing:
Australian organisations are being urged to address the growing risk posed by smart glasses capable of covert recording. Advocates are calling for a ban on devices that can film people without their knowledge, raising serious privacy concerns in workplaces, training environments, and public spaces. Staff should be aware that someone wearing ordinary-looking glasses may be recording without consent, which could breach privacy laws.

A newly identified technique called "GhostJacking" highlights security weaknesses in AI-powered systems, where attackers can manipulate automated agents by exploiting gaps in identity controls. Organisations using AI tools should ensure proper access controls are in place.

**Practical tip:** If you spot someone wearing unusual smart glasses in restricted or sensitive areas, report it to your manager or security team immediately.

featured.title: Australia urged to ban smart glasses over covert filming
featured.quote: Smart glasses covert filming poses serious privacy risks for Australian public spaces.
